summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of type 2 diabetes, kidney transplant, peripheral vascular disease, and prior toe amputations was admitted for fever and a chronic draining ulcer on his right fourth toe. Imaging revealed osteolysis suggestive of osteomyelitis. He underwent debridement and partial ostectomy of the infected bone. Initial broad-spectrum antibiotics were narrowed to ertapenem after wound cultures identified Citrobacter freundii, sensitive to most agents except Bactrim. A PICC line was placed for outpatient IV antibiotic therapy. His blood pressure was labile, prompting a switch from metoprolol to labetalol. Diabetes management was optimized with increased insulin dosing. Renal function remained stable, and he was discharged home with plans for weekly labs, infectious disease follow-up, and wound care.
